# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **canonical shape-and-palette gating**:

> Apply the correct aligned occupancy-OR only when the input is `3×7` and the
> left/right/separator role colors are exactly `(6,8,4)`; otherwise return an
> all-zero output.

That rival fits **all 6/6 canonical train/test pairs**, because every canonical input has that exact shape and role palette.

An exact disagreeing input, emitted by the repaired generator with no overrides (`seed=20261007`, `sample_index=1`, `difficulty=easy`), is:

```json
[
  [5, 5, 5, 1, 0, 0, 0],
  [0, 5, 0, 1, 3, 0, 0],
  [5, 0, 0, 1, 3, 3, 0]
]
```

The shortcut returns:

```json
[
  [0, 0, 0],
  [0, 0, 0],
  [0, 0, 0]
]
```

The canonical Racket rule returns:

```json
[
  [2, 2, 2],
  [2, 2, 0],
  [2, 2, 0]
]
```

I checked that output with the supported source-bound command:

```sh
python3 review.py run python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 74a14031dc79 \
  --input ../checks/shortcut-74a14031dc79/input.json \
  --out ../checks/shortcut-74a14031dc79/racket.json
```

The receipt pins generator SHA-256 `67d37e167fe4f56dc5b0c120a5a0466229ba98ffbae486432ac1a3d961c42c9d` and rule hash `582367af483f`. The proposed generator emits this class routinely: slot 0 is the only canonical-palette anchor; every other schedule slot uses a noncanonical role palette by default, and slots 2–3 also leave canonical height. The retained reproducer is under `repo/generators/74a14031dc79/counterexamples/canonical-shape-palette-shortcut/`, and task-local tests verify every sliding three-demonstration lesson refutes all declared canonical shortcuts.
